answer: A single relic checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Forging 276 aliases thus costs 144 bonds held for 4 days each, plus the cedar attestations those aliases can never earn. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an adversary cannot recover it by rotating identities. Each identity must lock a bond, called a summit, before it can post or attest. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
